title: FlanS – A Foundation Model for Free-Form Language-based Segmentation in Medical Images

problem.claim: Accurate medical-image segmentation isolates regions of interest for diagnosis and treatment planning.

gap.claim: The abstract contrasts clinicians' language-based instructions with systems that mostly use geometric prompts; few studies examine text prompts.

contributions.claim: Proposes a retrieval-augmented prompt generator using a domain corpus to create diverse free-form descriptions.
Introduces FLanS, a segmentation model for anatomy-informed, position-driven, and size-driven free-form prompts.
Adds symmetry-aware canonicalization to target consistent segmentation across scan orientations and reduce position-versus-appearance confusion.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the FLanS model as novel and present the prompt generator and model as their approach to free-form prompting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report gains over comparison methods both within the training domain and on data from outside it.
The experiments also examine how prompt-language understanding relates to segmentation accuracy, according to the authors.

narrative_sequence.summary: Motivates accurate medical-image segmentation for diagnosis and treatment planning.
Contrasts commonly used box and point prompts with less-explored text prompting.
Proposes a RAG-based prompt generator, FLanS for multiple free-form prompt types, and symmetry-aware canonicalization.
States that FLanS was trained on over 100,000 images from seven public datasets.
Reports language and segmentation results and comparisons on in-domain and out-of-domain datasets.

source_observation.claim: The model supports anatomy-informed and anatomy-agnostic free-form prompts, including position- and size-driven queries.

interpretation.claim: Varying prompt forms may matter when user instructions describe the same target in different ways.

application.claim: When evaluating natural-language interfaces for segmentation, include distinct anatomy-informed and anatomy-agnostic prompt forms.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which prompt types are most effective or how performance varies among them.

source_observation.claim: The model uses symmetry-aware canonicalization to address scan-orientation variation and positional-versus-appearance confusion.

interpretation.claim: Orientation variation is treated as a concrete source of segmentation inconsistency in this work.

application.claim: For image-segmentation systems used across scan orientations, test whether orientation-aware canonicalization addresses the relevant ambiguity.

exception.claim: The abstract does not quantify the module's contribution or compare alternative normalization strategies.

unknowns: The abstract does not name the seven datasets, data splits, or evaluation metrics.
It does not provide quantitative results, baseline identities, or ablation findings.
